newsitem.title: USA: Arkansas Supreme denies rehearing for gaming issue.
newsitem.headline: Arkansas Supreme denies rehearing for gaming issue.

text.p: The Arkansas State Supreme Court said Monday it denied a request for a rehearing sought by supporters of a proposed gambling amendment that it struck from the state's November ballot last week, court officials.
Clerk of the Court Leslie Steen said the court heard the request on Friday and announced its decision Monday.

Amendment 7 supporters last week petitioned the court both for a rehearing and to have a special justice dismissed from the case because of a "perceived conflict of interest," according to a release from the Committee to Promote Arkansas, which supports the amendment.
"The justice that they wanted to disqualify just responded to their motion and apparently the court did not act on the motion to disqualify," Steen said.

On Oct 21, the court said it ruled four to three to strike the amendment from the general election ballot because of ballot title problems. That same day, Amendment 7 supporters announced plans to file for a rehearing and to request Special Justice Sandra Smith Hochstetter's removal.
The release said Hochstetter is assistant general counsel for a business called Arkla Gas, which is represented by a lawfirm that also represents another gambling amendment, Amendment 4.

The court's decision means Amendment 7 will not get on the November ballot "unless the try and take it real quick to the United States Supreme Court," Daniel Dodson, a deputy clerk for the court said.
David Couch, an attorney representing Amendment 7 supporters, could not be reached immediately for comment.
